officialDocs.label: Configuring your environment for Sign in with Apple
Sign in with Apple REST API
Configure Sign in with Apple for the web

verdict.summary: Sign in with Apple is identity only: the only scopes are name and email (plus openid), and Apple offers no OAuth API for reading or writing user data such as iCloud Mail, Calendar, Contacts, Photos or Drive, so it can authenticate your agent's users but can't give the agent access to their Apple data. Setup is self-serve with no review for web sign-in, but it needs a paid Apple Developer Program membership ($99/year), an App ID plus Services ID, verified HTTPS domains (no localhost), and a JWT client secret you re-sign at least every 6 months.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Assumes an existing paid membership. Most of the time goes to the App ID, Services ID, private key and JWT client secret, and to an HTTPS tunnel or staging domain, since localhost return URLs are rejected. A new organization enrollment (D-U-N-S, identity verification) can add days or more.

timeToProd.assumes: Web sign-in for an agent product whose users already have a membership-backed App ID and Services ID. It doesn't cover user-data access, which Apple doesn't offer via OAuth.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Nothing — no review for web sign-in. New organizations wait on Apple Developer Program enrollment verification, and iOS apps go through normal App Review.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: No Sign in with Apple-specific review is documented for websites. Apple's environment doc says web authentication needs an existing App Store app using Sign in with Apple, which we couldn't confirm is enforced.

verdict.cost: Apple Developer Program membership, 99 USD per membership year (prices may vary by region).

prerequisites.item: A paid Apple Developer Program membership (Account Holder or Admin role)
prerequisites.why: Identifiers, keys and the Sign in with Apple capability are configured in Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles, which is a program feature. Configuring it needs the Account Holder or Admin role.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The membership requirement is our reading of the program pages. The help article states the role requirement but not the membership.

prerequisites.item: For organizations: a D-U-N-S Number, a legal entity (no DBAs), a public website on your domain, and an Account Holder with signing authority
prerequisites.why: Apple verifies the organization's identity and legal status before enrollment completes.

prerequisites.item: A primary App ID with Sign in with Apple enabled (Apple's doc says an existing App Store app)
prerequisites.why: Services IDs (web client IDs) and private keys are tied to a primary App ID. The doc says web authentication requires an existing App Store app that uses Sign in with Apple.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Many web-only integrations appear to use an unpublished primary App ID. We didn't verify whether the App Store requirement is enforced.

prerequisites.item: Verified HTTPS domains and absolute return URLs (no localhost, no IP addresses)
prerequisites.why: redirect_uri must use HTTPS, include a domain name, and can't be an IP address or localhost. All domains and subdomains have to be registered and verified on the Services ID.

prerequisites.item: SPF/DKIM-authenticated outbound email domains, if you email users
prerequisites.why: Users can hide their email behind the Private Email Relay. Mail to relay addresses is delivered only from registered, authenticated sources.

scopeTiers.impact: You get a stable pairwise user ID (sub), and optionally name and a real or relay email. If you request any scope, response_mode must be form_post. Apple returns no API-usable access to user content.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: The live discovery document lists scopes_supported [openid, email, name] and subject_types [pairwise].

scopeTiers.tier: User data (mail, calendar, contacts, files): not available via OAuth
scopeTiers.impact: There are no public OAuth scopes for iCloud data. Third-party iCloud Mail/Calendar/Contacts access normally uses IMAP/CalDAV/CardDAV with a user-generated app-specific password (2FA required). Apple mentions 'supported' apps that can authorize with an Apple Account instead, but no developer program for that is documented.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Inferred from the discovery document and the app-specific password support page. We found no developer docs for OAuth access to iCloud data.

scopeTiers.impact: A separate Apple product for education apps that reads Apple School Manager user and class data. It isn't general consumer data. Its use depends on the school or organization sharing data with your app.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: reviewRequired=true is our inference: organization data sharing depends on the organization's admin, and Apple's onboarding path wasn't reviewed in depth.

steps.title: Enroll in the Apple Developer Program
steps.detail: Enroll as an individual or organization (organizations need a D-U-N-S Number, a legal entity, a public website on their domain, and an Account Holder with signing authority). Pay 99 USD per year.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The duration is our estimate. Apple states no processing time.

steps.title: Enable Sign in with Apple on a primary App ID
steps.detail: In Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles > Identifiers, create or edit an App ID, tick Sign in with Apple, and choose 'Enable as a primary App ID'.

steps.title: Create a Services ID with domains and return URLs
steps.detail: Register a Services ID (this is your web client_id), enable Sign in with Apple, link it to the primary App ID, and add verified domains and absolute HTTPS return URLs. Organizations can register up to 100 website URLs, individuals up to 10.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: The Services ID console URL returned 302 to idmsa.apple.com sign-in on 2026-10-20. We did not sign in.

steps.title: Create a Sign in with Apple private key
steps.detail: Under Keys, create a key with Sign in with Apple enabled for the primary App ID. Download the .p8 file (it can be downloaded only once) and note the Key ID and Team ID. Each primary app can have at most two keys.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The one-time download is from Apple's key help page, not re-checked here.

steps.title: Generate the JWT client secret
steps.detail: Sign an ES256 JWT with header kid=<Key ID> and claims iss=<Team ID>, iat, exp (at most 15777000 seconds, about 6 months, ahead), aud=https://appleid.apple.com, sub=<Services ID>. Schedule automatic re-signing before exp.

steps.title: Implement the authorization request and token exchange
steps.detail: Redirect to https://appleid.apple.com/auth/authorize?client_id=<Services ID>&redirect_uri=<https>&response_type=code&response_mode=form_post&scope=name%20email&state=...&nonce=.... Handle the POST callback, then exchange the code (single-use, valid 5 minutes) at POST https://appleid.apple.com/auth/token with client_secret_post.

steps.title: Validate the ID token and persist name/email on first sign-in
steps.detail: Verify the id_token against https://appleid.apple.com/auth/keys (iss, aud, exp, nonce). Store sub as the user key. Save the user's name from the callback's user JSON on first authorization, because Apple doesn't return it again.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: The JWKS and claims are sourced. 'Name only on first authorization' is widely reported by developers but wasn't confirmed in the pages we read.

steps.title: Register email sources and server-to-server notifications
steps.detail: Add outbound email domains/addresses for the Private Email Relay (authenticate with SPF and DKIM), and register a TLS 1.2+ endpoint for account-change notifications.

steps.title: Handle consent-revoked, account-deleted and token revocation
steps.detail: Verify notification JWS payloads and act on email-disabled, email-enabled, consent-revoked and account-deleted events. When a user deletes their account in your product, call POST https://appleid.apple.com/auth/revoke with their refresh or access token.

steps.title: Plan a separate path for Apple user data, if needed
steps.detail: If the agent needs iCloud mail, calendar or contacts, don't plan on OAuth. The documented route is IMAP/CalDAV/CardDAV with a user-created app-specific password, which has security and UX trade-offs to weigh with the product owner.

agentCanDo: Generate and rotate the ES256 client-secret JWT
Implement authorize, token, ID-token verification and revoke
Probe the discovery document and JWKS
humanMustDo: Enroll in and pay for the Apple Developer Program
Create the App ID, Services ID and private key
Verify domains and register email relay sources
Keep the .p8 key safe and choose the key holder

blockers.cause: The client secret JWT is wrong or expired (bad kid, iss, sub, aud, or exp more than 15777000 s ahead), or client_id doesn't match the Services ID.
blockers.fix: Re-sign the JWT with the correct Key ID, Team ID and Services ID as sub, and set exp within 6 months.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: POST /auth/token with no params returned {"error":"invalid_client"} on 2026-10-20. Mapping it to JWT mistakes is inferred.

blockers.symptom: Return URL rejected when testing on http://localhost
blockers.cause: redirect_uri can't be localhost or an IP address and must be HTTPS with a domain.
blockers.fix: Use an HTTPS tunnel or a staging domain registered on the Services ID.

blockers.symptom: Authorize fails when requesting name/email with response_mode=query
blockers.cause: If any scope is requested, response_mode must be form_post.
blockers.fix: Use response_mode=form_post and accept a POST on the return URL.

blockers.cause: Your sending domain or address isn't registered as an email source, or lacks SPF/DKIM.
blockers.fix: Register the email sources in the developer account and authenticate them with SPF and DKIM.

blockers.symptom: Users report the app can't see their iCloud mail or calendar
blockers.cause: Sign in with Apple grants identity only. No OAuth scope exists for iCloud data.
blockers.fix: Set expectations in the product, or offer a separate IMAP/CalDAV connection with app-specific passwords.

blockers.cause: The app offers a third-party login (such as Google) for the primary account without an equivalent privacy-focused option.
blockers.fix: Add Sign in with Apple (or another login meeting 4.8's criteria), unless an exemption applies.

nuances.text: Authorization codes are single-use and valid for 5 minutes. The token response has an ID token, an access token and a refresh token. Refreshing returns a new ID token and access token, which verify the session but unlock no data APIs.
The client secret is a JWT you sign yourself with a lifetime of at most 6 months, so an expired secret breaks every sign-in until it's re-signed.
User IDs are pairwise (team-scoped), and users can hide their email behind a relay address. Don't use email as the primary key.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: subject_types_supported [pairwise] and the is_private_email claim are in the live discovery document.

nuances.text: App grouping under a primary App ID means users consent once per group of apps and websites, and their credentials are shared across the group.
Each primary app can have at most two private keys, which allows rotation. Revoke a compromised key after moving to the new one.
On iOS, guideline 4.8 can make Sign in with Apple (or an equivalent) mandatory if you also offer Google or other social login for the primary account.
